To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a 1 year moderate-to-high training in patients following myocardium infarction can induce a significant improvement of exercise induced ischemia.
a 1 year moderate-to-high training programme in some patients following a myocardial infarct can elicit adaptations which may be attributed, at leat in part, to improvement of coronary blood flow.
exercise training can improve the ischemic threshold in some patients after myocardial ischemia.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the evaluation of the effect of a 12-month exercise training programme on exercise-induced myocardial ischemia.
the evaluation of the effects of a 1-yr moderate-to-high exercise training program in patients with previous myocardial infarctions.
the effects of exercise on the myocardium of patients with coronary artery disease.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
a 1 year exercise training program is able to improve myocardial ischemia.
exercise training can be recommended for patients with coronary heart disease, provided that they can exercise without symptoms.
exercise training is safe and beneficial for patients with coronary artery disease, and that it should be considered as part of their rehabilitation program.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

exercise training is an effective and safe therapy in the management of patients with ischemic heart disease, and that it can improve the functional status of patients and decrease morbidity and mortality.
the exercise training program is a safe, effective, and inexpensive means to reduce the symptoms of angina and to improve the exercise capacity in patients after myocardium infarction.

exercise training is an effective and safe method to reduce myocardial ischemia and to improve exercise capacity and quality of life in post-myocardial infarction patients with stable angina pectoris.
The main takeaway from our work is that
exercise is an effective and safe way to reduce the risk of heart disease and stroke, and it can be used in combination with other treatments to help prevent these conditions.
exercise training may improve coronary blood flow, and thus, the exercise-induced myocardial ischemia.
exercise is a very important part of the rehabilitation process after a heart attack.
